food_bismillah.title: Before Eating
food_bismillah.benefit: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: When any one of you eats, let him mention the name of Allah. This is the Sunnah act before every meal.

food_bismillah_forgot.title: If You Forgot Bismillah
food_bismillah_forgot.translation: In the name of Allah at its beginning and at its end.
food_bismillah_forgot.benefit: If you forget to say Bismillah at the start, say this as soon as you remember — even mid-meal. The Prophet (ﷺ) instructed this so the entire meal is covered by the blessing.
food_bismillah_forgot.occasion: Recite immediately when you remember you forgot Bismillah.

food_allahumma_barik_eating.title: Before Eating (Extended — Da'if)
food_allahumma_barik_eating.arabicText: اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لَنَا فِيمَا رَزَقْتَنَا وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
food_allahumma_barik_eating.transliteration: Allāhumma bārik lanā fīmā razaqtanā wa qinā 'adhāban-nār
food_allahumma_barik_eating.translation: O Allah, bless us in what You have provided for us and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
food_allahumma_barik_eating.benefit: Widely recited before meals. Its chain is classified as weak (Da'if), but the meaning is sound and scholars permit its use as a general supplication. An authentic alternative is recommended — see dua #4.
food_allahumma_barik_eating.reference: Ibn as-Sunni — Amal al-Yawm wal-Lailah 457 | At-Tabarani

food_allahumma_barik_fihi.title: Authentic Du'a When Food Is Brought
food_allahumma_barik_fihi.arabicText: اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لَنَا فِيهِ وَأَطْعِمْنَا خَيْرًا مِنْهُ
food_allahumma_barik_fihi.transliteration: Allāhumma bārik lanā fīhi wa at'imnā khayran minhu
food_allahumma_barik_fihi.translation: O Allah, bless us in it and feed us with what is better than it.
food_allahumma_barik_fihi.benefit: This is a highly authentic du'a taught by the Prophet (ﷺ) specifically when food is brought. Graded Hasan (sound). It is a recommended authentic alternative to the more widely known but weaker dua before eating.
food_allahumma_barik_fihi.occasion: Recite when food is placed before you.

food_alhamdulillah_long.title: After Eating (Full — Most Rewarding)
food_alhamdulillah_long.arabicText: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنِي هَذَا وَرَزَقَنِيهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ حَوْلٍ مِنِّي وَلَا قُوَّةٍ
food_alhamdulillah_long.transliteration: Al-hamdu lillāhil-ladhī at'amanī hādhā wa razaqanīhi min ghayri hawlin minnī wa lā quwwatin
food_alhamdulillah_long.translation: All praise is due to Allah who fed me this and provided it for me without any power or strength on my part.
food_alhamdulillah_long.benefit: The Prophet (ﷺ) said whoever recites this after eating will have his past sins forgiven. This is the most rewarding post-meal dua. Graded Hasan by Imam Al-Albani.
food_alhamdulillah_long.reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 4023 | Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3458 | Sunan Ibn Majah 3285

food_alhamdulillah_short.title: After Eating (Short — Widely Used)
food_alhamdulillah_short.arabicText: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنَا وَسَقَانَا وَجَعَلَنَا مُسْلِمِينَ
food_alhamdulillah_short.transliteration: Al-hamdu lillāhil-ladhī at'amanā wa saqānā wa ja'alanā muslimīn
food_alhamdulillah_short.translation: All praise is due to Allah who fed us, gave us to drink, and made us Muslims.
food_alhamdulillah_short.benefit: Widely used by classical scholars including Imam An-Nawawi. Contemporary hadith scholars including Al-Albani have noted its chain is weak (Da'if). It remains permissible due to its excellent meaning. For a stronger narration, prefer the longer dua above.
food_alhamdulillah_short.reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 3850 | Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3457 | Sunan Ibn Majah 3283
food_alhamdulillah_short.grading: Da'if (permissible — excellent meaning, relied upon by Imam An-Nawawi)

food_guest_dua.title: When Eating as a Guest
food_guest_dua.arabicText: اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لَهُمْ فِيمَا رَزَقْتَهُمْ، وَاغْفِرْ لَهُمْ، وَارْحَمْهُمْ
food_guest_dua.transliteration: Allāhumma bārik lahum fīmā razaqtahum, waghfir lahum, warhamhum
food_guest_dua.translation: O Allah, bless them in what You have provided for them, forgive them, and have mercy on them.
food_guest_dua.benefit: This is a Sahih dua from Sahih Muslim. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to supplicate for the hosts when he ate at their home. Making this dua is a beautiful act of gratitude and a gift to your host.
food_guest_dua.occasion: Recite after eating as a guest at someone's home.
